This strategic failure allowed Apple to secure a monopoly, leaving labels without alternative distribution channels when the iPod eventually lost its dominance.", "summary": "Record labels' strategic reliance on Apple caused them to miss the window for developing high-quality music formats before the iPod monopoly collapsed."}, "13": {"original": "Apps fail to match the quality of music, as downloading tracks to phones doesn't", "rephrased": "Current mobile applications are ill-suited for music distribution because they cannot deliver the high-fidelity audio quality that dedicated music players provide, rendering the single-track format insufficient for the listening experience. While app-based models offer a potential future for the industry, the technology currently lacks the audio performance required to replace the traditional album format effectively.", "summary": "Mobile apps currently fail to match the high-fidelity audio quality of dedicated music players, limiting their viability as a replacement for the album format."}, "14": {"original": "It doesn't make up for the fall in CD sales, but increasingly it looks like noth", "rephrased": "Digital downloads have failed to compensate for the massive decline in CD sales, and the music industry's most profitable era appears to be permanently behind it. However, a shift toward an app-based economy, where artists sell premium content directly to mobile users, offers a viable path forward for recording companies to find new growth drivers.", "summary": "While digital downloads failed to save the music industry from CD decline, a shift to app-based direct sales offers a potential new growth strategy."}, "15": {"original": "Nine Inch Nails released their first app in April 2009.", "rephrased": "The industrial rock band Nine Inch Nails demonstrated early industry adaptation by releasing their first dedicated mobile application in April 2009, signaling that major artists were beginning to explore app-based revenue streams to bypass traditional record label structures.", "summary": "Nine Inch Nails released their first mobile app in April 2009, marking an early instance of artists exploring app-based revenue models."}}
